guided.title: Name the class
guided.prompt: Write `status_class(code)` that returns `"2xx"`, `"3xx"`, `"4xx"`, `"5xx"` (or `"1xx"`) from an integer code using integer division. Print the class for `[200, 204, 301, 404, 429, 503]` on one line separated by spaces. Expected output: `2xx 2xx 3xx 4xx 4xx 5xx`.
hints: Integer division by 100 keeps the first digit.
Build the text from that digit and the letters `xx`.

guided.title: Should a pipeline retry?
guided.prompt: Write `should_retry(code)` that returns `True` for `429` and for any 5xx code, and `False` for everything else. Print the results for `[200, 401, 404, 429, 500, 503]` as a list. Expected output: `[False, False, False, True, True, True]`.
hints: A 4xx code means the request is wrong, with one exception.
The 5xx class starts at 500 and ends before 600.

guided.title: PUT replaces the whole record
guided.prompt: The dictionary `store` holds order 2. Write `put(store, order_id, body)` that replaces the stored record with `body` plus the key `order_id`, and a `patch` that would merge instead (only `put` is required). Call `put` with `{"amount_cents": 700}`, then print the stored record with sorted keys as a list of items. Expected output: `[('amount_cents', 700), ('order_id', 2)]`.
hints: Replacing means the old fields are not kept.
Assign a new dictionary to the key instead of updating the old one.

guided.title: Read Retry-After
guided.prompt: Write `wait_seconds(headers)` that returns the integer in the `Retry-After` header (the lookup must work for any capitalisation of the name, so lower-case the keys first) and `1` when the header is missing or is not a whole number. Print the results for the four header dictionaries given. Expected output: `2`, `30`, `1`, `1`.
hints: Header names are case-insensitive, so normalise them before the lookup.
`str.isdigit()` tells whether the text is a whole number.
Return `int(value)` when the text is digits, otherwise `1`.

independent.title: Summarise a run's status codes
independent.prompt: The list `codes` holds the status codes of one pipeline run. Print four lines: `2xx 6` style counts per class for the classes that occur, in ascending order of class (`2xx`, `4xx`, ...); then `retryable: ` and the number of codes for which a retry is sensible (429 or 5xx); then `client errors: ` and the sorted list of distinct 4xx codes other than 429. Expected output: `2xx 6`, `4xx 3`, `5xx 2`, `retryable: 4`, `client errors: [401, 404]`.

independent.title: A tiny API in a function
independent.prompt: Write `handle(store, method, path, body=None)` returning `(status, body)` for a store that maps order ids to dictionaries. `GET /orders/<id>` gives `(200, record)` or `(404, {"error": "not found"})`; `POST /orders` with a `customer_id` in the body creates a record with id `max(store) + 1` and returns `(201, record)`, without `customer_id` it returns `(422, {"error": "customer_id is required"})`; `DELETE /orders/<id>` returns `(204, None)` or `(404, ...)`. Run the six calls given and print `status` for each followed by the sorted store keys. Expected output: six status lines and the key list.
independent.expected:
GET /orders/1 200
GET /orders/9 404
POST /orders 201
POST /orders 422
DELETE /orders/2 204
DELETE /orders/2 404
[1, 3]

independent.title: Retry policy by status
independent.prompt: Write a short retry policy for an ingestion job that only reads with GET: for each of 200, 301, 400, 401, 403, 404, 429, 500, 503 say what the job does and why. Then say what changes if the job writes with POST.
independent.solution: 200: use the body. 301: follow the redirect (requests does for GET) and update the configured URL. 400: the request is malformed; stop and fix the parameters, since repeating it fails again. 401: the key is missing or invalid; stop and alert, retrying wastes calls. 403: the key is valid but not permitted; stop and ask for access. 404: the resource does not exist; log it and continue with the next id or stop, depending on whether the id was expected. 429: wait for Retry-After and retry, within a limit. 500 and 503: temporary server trouble; retry with a growing wait and give up after a few attempts, then report. With POST the same classes apply, but a timeout or a 5xx does not tell whether the record was created, so retrying risks a duplicate unless the request carries an idempotency key or the job first checks whether the record exists.
rubric: Does not retry 400, 401, 403 and gives the reason
Retries 429 and 5xx with a wait and a limit
Explains the duplicate risk for POST

checks.question: Which method is NOT idempotent?
checks.explanation: Each POST creates another resource, so repeating it changes the server again. GET, PUT and DELETE leave the server in the same state however many times the same request repeats.

checks.question: A request returns 401. What is the most sensible reaction in a pipeline?
options: Stop and fix the credentials, because the same request will fail again
checks.explanation: 401 says the server does not accept the credentials, so repeating the same request cannot succeed. The retry classes are 429 and 5xx.

checks.question: What is the difference between 401 and 403?
options: 401: credentials missing or invalid; 403: credentials valid but not allowed
checks.explanation: 401 concerns identity and 403 concerns permission. Both are 4xx, so retrying unchanged will not help.

checks.question: After `PUT /orders/2` with the body `{"amount_cents": 700}`, what does the stored order contain in a REST API that follows the rules?
options: Only the fields sent, plus the id
checks.explanation: PUT replaces the whole resource, so fields not in the body are gone. PATCH is the method for changing only some fields.

checks.question: What does `response.raise_for_status()` do for a 404?
checks.explanation: It raises an exception for 4xx and 5xx statuses and does nothing for success codes. It does not retry; that logic is yours (Day 107).

environment.note: Example 4 sends real HTTP requests with the requests library to a throwaway http.server on 127.0.0.1 started in a thread, so it runs locally after `pip install requests` and is shown read-only in the browser. No real service is contacted. The graded exercises reproduce the logic (methods, status classes, retry decisions, header parsing) with plain functions and dictionaries that run in the browser.
